title: Photo Studio
summary: A photography workspace with 24 desktop effects, foreground segmentation, and a browser playground.
steps: Choose a photograph
Use a bundled animal or nature sample, or open a local image in the browser companion.
Explore the effects
Compare the original with color, tonal, edge, and segmentation effects. The desktop app contains all 24 operations; the browser companion contains 10.
Keep the result
Download the browser preview as PNG, or use the desktop app for full-resolution batch exports.
limitation: The browser companion previews a subset of the desktop effects. GrabCut foreground extraction runs in the Python desktop app.

title: Iron Tide
summary: A Silent Hunter–inspired Atlantic patrol: find the convoy, line up the shot, and escape the escort.
steps: Begin patrol
Enter the patrol briefing and sail toward the convoy.
Find a firing solution
Switch between the external view, attack periscope, and tactical chart to track contacts.
Stay alive
Manage depth, propulsion, and torpedo attacks while evading the destroyer.
limitation: Requires a desktop keyboard and a browser with WebGL. This is a fictional game rather than a historical simulator.

title: PROP//WASH
summary: FPV drone flight over real satellite imagery and elevation, with race gates and a physics-driven battery model.
steps: Pick the terrain
Choose among seven real locations, from the Grand Canyon to Bora Bora.
Take the controls
Fly with keyboard or gamepad in self-leveling ANGLE mode or direct-rate ACRO mode.
Race or explore
Fly the gates, hunt targets, or watch the demo autopilot. Satellite tiles stream during play.
limitation: Real terrain depends on external imagery and elevation services. The simulator uses procedural terrain if those services are unavailable. Keyboard/gamepad and WebGL are recommended.

title: Empathy CAPTCHA
summary: A satirical human-or-replicant interrogation, told through escalating CAPTCHA challenges and behavioral signals.
steps: Take the baseline
Start the fictional interrogation. The game observes reaction timing and input movement locally.
Meet the challenges
Solve selections, drawing tasks, and other escalating CAPTCHA parodies.
Read your verdict
Inspect the fictional verdict and download a session transcript from the original app.
limitation: A parody, not a real CAPTCHA or psychological assessment. The original app keeps session data in the browser.

title: Learning to land
summary: DQN and PPO agents learn controlled spacecraft landings in Gymnasium's LunarLander-v3.
steps: Observe the state
The agent receives lander position, velocity, angle, and ground-contact observations.
Learn a policy
Compare a value-based DQN with PPO's clipped policy updates using the repository's PyTorch implementations.
Evaluate the flight
Watch actual repository recordings and inspect the saved reward curves.
limitation: The animations are recorded trained-agent episodes. Training and inference require the Python/Gymnasium environment.

title: A drone learning to fly
summary: A modular Gymnasium environment for quadrotor hover, waypoint tracking, obstacle navigation, and depth-camera perception.
steps: Choose the task
Configure hover, waypoints, trajectory tracking, or navigation with point-mass or six-degree-of-freedom physics.
Train with a curriculum
Use PPO and success-based difficulty changes to introduce increasingly dense obstacle fields.
Inspect the behavior
Watch recorded hover and navigation episodes; compare the state-based and depth-camera interfaces.
limitation: Hover footage is a 50,000-step smoke-test policy that eventually drifts. A recorded successful navigation run does not imply universal success.

title: Finding the way through
summary: Curriculum-trained PPO and Dueling Double DQN navigate two-, four-, and six-room MiniGrid mazes.
steps: See only part of the map
The agent observes a small local grid, while layouts and doors change between episodes.
Build up the difficulty
Transfer learning through small, medium, and large rooms, using rewards that discourage door-cycling.
Compare the policies
Inspect recorded PPO and D3QN runs, including a documented failure case.
limitation: These are saved agent recordings, not a model running in this page. Evaluation figures describe the original experiments.

title: Flappy Bird, trained
summary: Q-learning and SARSA learn when to flap, then face narrower pipe gaps to test generalization.
steps: Discretize the world
Reduce positions and velocities to a compact tabular state space.
Learn from the reward
Compare off-policy Q-learning with on-policy SARSA under the same reward shaping.
Change the difficulty
Watch the original trained recordings at different pipe gaps alongside the random baseline.
limitation: Recorded agents use the original project's environment. Performance depends on the training gap and evaluation setup.

title: Inside the auction
summary: A 249,000-impression real-time bidding analysis: click drivers, auction behavior, and calibrated win-rate pricing.
steps: Decode the event
Inspect the auction, placement, device, and structural missingness before fitting a model.
Separate the questions
Study traffic quality and click propensity separately from the market's bid landscape.
Calibrate the bid
Use the hierarchical quantile model and back-test target versus realized win rates.
limitation: Saved figures describe one dataset and its back-test. This page does not price live ad inventory.

title: Which language is this?
summary: Character n-grams and perplexity turn language identification into a question of which model is least surprised.
steps: Build the character models
Count character n-grams for English, Spanish, French, Indonesian, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, and Tagalog.
Score the text
Sum log probabilities and normalize by text length to calculate perplexity.
Pick the lowest score
Compare the language models. Try the small, explicitly illustrative browser port below.
limitation: The browser version trains on short, newly written sample sentences, not the repository's tweet corpus. Its scores are illustrative and unreliable on short or unfamiliar text.

title: A small poetry machine
summary: Second-order Markov transitions assemble new lines one word at a time, with the previous two words as context.
steps: Read the corpus
The original Python project learns transition counts from Robert Frost's poetry.
Follow the transitions
Sample an initial word, a second word, then the next word conditioned on the preceding pair.
Write a new line
Try the same kind of algorithm in the browser using a small original nature-themed corpus.
limitation: This browser port uses newly written sample text. It is not the original Frost-trained model and does not run a neural language model.

title: Find evidence before answering
summary: Wikipedia question answering combines BM25 and QLD retrieval, BGE reranking, and few-shot generation.
steps: Retrieve candidate passages
Fuse lexical BM25 and query-likelihood retrieval across entity and question variants.
Rerank the evidence
A BGE cross-encoder scores query/passage pairs before context assembly.
Generate and retry
The original pipeline calls a deployed LLM and retries suspicious or empty answers with more context.
limitation: The browser experiment is BM25 over five original sample passages. It does not load Wikipedia, a BGE model, or a hosted LLM.

title: What deserves the top result?
summary: BM25, RM3 expansion, and QLD plus BGE reranking compete on the ROBUST04 news collection.
steps: Retrieve broadly
Find lexical candidates from 528,030 documents using BM25 or query likelihood.
Rerank carefully
Compare RM3 pseudo-relevance feedback, cross-encoder reranking, and LambdaMART.
Measure the ranking
Inspect the repository's per-query AP and method comparison figures; training and test results tell different stories.
limitation: The sample BM25 below demonstrates lexical retrieval only. Published figures refer to the original ROBUST04 experiments, not these sample passages.

title: Tiny memory, streaming signals
summary: Five compact sketches monitor token-distribution changes as LLM output arrives.
steps: Build a reference profile
Summarize trusted text with Count-Min Sketch, HyperLogLog++, AMS, Bloom Filter, and MinHash.
Stream the output
Measure vocabulary, concentration, frequency, membership, and n-gram divergence.
Evaluate the detector
Inspect the original F1-versus-memory figures. The browser component demonstrates Count-Min Sketch counting.
limitation: The Count-Min Sketch demo estimates token frequencies; it does not determine whether a claim is true. Reported detector performance belongs to the repository's evaluation.

title: When training data changes the story
summary: A literary model study separates style corruption from factual knowledge poisoning, using GPT-2 and Llama.
steps: Define the attack
Modify literary training material or factual question-answer data.
Fine-tune and probe
Compare Tolkien-style generation and Harry Potter knowledge before and after poisoning.
Distinguish change from learning
Measure changed answers and detected poison indicators; instability is different from successfully learning the intended false fact.
limitation: This page presents saved study figures. It neither fine-tunes a model nor generates poisoned text in the browser.

title: Detecting attacks in a stream
summary: Probabilistic sketches compress network-flow windows before attack classification on UNSW-NB15.
steps: Window the events
Group network flows into 30-second tumbling windows.
Compress the statistics
Morris, FM, AMS, Count-Min, and Count-Sketch summarize volume, diversity, and concentration.
Classify the window
Compare approximate sketch features with exact baselines. Try frequency estimation on a small local stream below.
limitation: The browser component demonstrates sketch counting, not network intrusion detection. The original classifier needs the UNSW-NB15 data and Python runtime.

title: Finding automated login patterns

Use timestamps, hashed identifiers, network metadata, and status codes.
Look for patterns
Explore bursts, high-volume sources, tool clusters, and unusual network combinations.
Inspect the findings
Compare the original aggregate risk and temporal figures before following up on suspicious sources.
limitation: This is a saved analysis, not a live attack monitor. Hashes, raw account records, and credentials are not republished here.

Evaluate classification

limitation: This page shows aggregate research artifacts, not an email gateway or a production DLP product. No individual email bodies are displayed.

Use the original training and performance plots to examine precision, recall, and F1.
